title: AI-guided CORONA imagery search finds four archaeologically verified tells in Abu Ghraib
summary: A fine-tuned deep-learning model trained with 1960s CORONA satellite images flagged eight previously unrecognized tell candidates in Iraq's Abu Ghraib district. Archaeologists investigated all eight; four contained surface ceramic sherds confirming archaeological remains and enabling dating. The AI suggestions led the field team to inspect locations that routine surveys would not have visited.
ai_technology: MANet deep convolutional segmentation network with attention, transfer learning and two-stage fine-tuning

evidence.tested: A fine-tuned deep-learning model trained with 1960s CORONA satellite images flagged eight previously unrecognized tell candidates in Iraq's Abu Ghraib district.
evidence.unknown: This is an arXiv preprint. The results are limited to mounded tell sites in Abu Ghraib and depend on a small training set (208 images) and archaeologist-selected field follow-up. Four of eight AI-suggested sites were confirmed; the other four should not be described as archaeological finds. The source reports that the four confirmed sites were destroyed or no longer visible on the ground, with sherds establishing their presence and dates.
evidence.ai_role: Researchers retrained the existing neural model using CORONA historical imagery and generated probability heatmaps that archaeologists used to select previously unrecognized locations for field reconnaissance. Eight AI-suggested sites were investigated; four were confirmed through collected and studied ceramic sherds. The authors state the four locations would not have been investigated in routine field surveys without the model's suggestions.
